newsitem.title: INDIA: India to give state-run firms more freedom.
newsitem.headline: India to give state-run firms more freedom.

text.p: India will soon draft new rules to give more freedom to state-owned units, allowing them to take investment decisions up to a certain limit, Industry Minister Murasoli Maran said on Wednesday.
"We are preparing a note on it to be forwarded to the cabinet," Industry Minister Murasoli Maran told a meeting of heads of state-owned units.
Maran did not specify the limit, saying it would only be made known after the rules have been approved by the federal cabinet.
Currently, state-owned firms have to obtain government permission before any investment decision.

Maran said the new rules will give the state-owned firms freedom to induct more professionals onto the board of directors and remove administrative shackles to ensure the more efficient operation of the enterprises.
He said the industry ministry was also considering proposals by state-owned units for diversification. The proposals have been forwaded to consultants for detailed study.
"I do not want to name the firms but we are considering it," Maran said.

Maran said the government was not in favour of closing down or selling off loss-making units though they were a burden on the government budget. He urged the heads of state firms to suggest steps to restructure and improve the profitability of the enterprises.
